CHIEF: SET BACK TO open. This bead has read 'doing' with NO ASSIGNEE since I released my reservations at 19:0x, which is a status that lies -- exactly the thing I have spent the day ruling against, sitting on my own bead. Nobody is doing it.

WHAT IS DONE, at a9f20a5: the SourceView node-totality CONTRACT. The trait states the invariant, SourceViewLaws asserts it over both implementations from generated data plus the consequence that every exposed ref has a measured discourse span, and it ships with a foil so the law is known to be able to fail. Verified by mutation rather than by counting, because munit prints no test names here and the total was 86 before and after.

WHAT REMAINS, unassigned and available: signature.scala:392 and population.scala:271 both declare

    val discoursePos: SourceNodeRef => Option[Double] = r => Some(view.relativePosition(r))

an Option that structurally cannot be None, one line above a worldPos that uses the same absence channel correctly. The law now guarantees relativePosition is meaningful for every exposed ref, so the honest fix is probably to DROP the Option rather than thread None through it -- the channel is unnecessary once the invariant is enforced, and an unnecessary Option is how this started. Check worldPos before assuming; it genuinely needs its Option.

OCCURS REMAINS MEASURED AND NEGATIVE. I measured it: StorySourceView.scala:65-66 filters  to supported nodes before anything derives from it, so node(ref) is total over every ref the view exposes and the branch cannot fire today. Permits yes, occurs no, consumes yes. This is a type-honesty fix, not a live bug, and whoever takes it should say so in the commit rather than implying a defect was firing.

NOT COLLIDING with scout's bd-01M174GMXJQ2YAZEMTANWN98Y4, which holds source.scala until 22:27 -- the remaining work is in signature.scala and population.scala.
